topics.title: Enter the two-factor authentication code
topics.text:
Two-factor authentication protects an account with a 6-digit code. This code changes every 30 seconds in an app on your phone (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password…).
If it is turned on for your account, the Two-Factor Authentication screen appears after the password:
Open the authenticator app on your phone.
Read the 6-digit code shown for your account.
Enter it in the Verification Code field.
Click Verify.
If something goes wrong, click Back to Login to start over.
Tip: if the message Invalid verification code appears, check that the phone's time is correct: a phone that is running late produces wrong codes. A code works only once: wait for the next one if you just used it.
Warning: wrong codes count as login attempts. After 5 errors in a row, the account is locked for 15 minutes.
The store can require two-factor authentication for people who manage users, roles, settings, or the audit log. In that case, the app sends you to Account security to turn it on before doing anything else (see Turn on two-factor authentication).

topics.title: Create your store
topics.text:
On some servers, the sign-in page offers New here? Create a store. This page creates a new store and makes you its Owner.
On the sign-in page, click Create a store.
Enter the Store name.
Enter your First name, Last name, Email and a Password (at least 8 characters).
Check the main Currency (3-letter code, for example USD or HTG).
Click Create store.
The app sets up a branch, a register and the Cash and Card payment methods for you. You then land in the app, signed in as the owner.
Tip: if you already have an account (in another store), enter the same email and password: the new store is added to your account. If that account uses two-factor authentication, the code is requested. You can then switch from one store to another in Account security (see Invitations and switching stores).
Warning: if the message "Sign-up is not available on this server. Ask your administrator for an account." appears, store creation is closed. Ask your administrator for an account.
Recommended next steps:
Fill in the General settings and the Business information.
Check the exchange rate.
Create your products or import them.
Add your staff.

topics.title: Understand roles
topics.text:
Each user is given a role. The role decides which menus are visible and which actions are allowed. Roles can be viewed in Admin > Roles & permissions (owner and administrator).
Role · For whom · What it can do · What it cannot do
Owner · The store's boss · Everything, including managing other owners. This role cannot be changed. · —
Admin · The owner's right hand · Manage everything: sales, stock, settings, staff accounts, roles, devices. · Edit or remove an owner.
Manager · The day-to-day store manager · Sell, void, refund, manage all shifts, approve variances, discounts and prices, manage products, stock, purchasing, customers, reports, settings. · Manage staff accounts, roles, devices and system monitoring.
Cashier · Till staff · Sell, give discounts up to the store limit, put sales on hold, open and close their own shift, record expenses, find and create customers, make estimates, view stock, reprint a receipt. · Change a price, go over the discount limit, sell on credit, make cash movements, refund, void. These actions need a manager's approval.
Inventory clerk · The stock person · Receive, adjust, count and transfer stock, manage suppliers, purchase orders and products. · Sell: no access to the till.
Accountant · The accountant · Dashboard, reports and exports, sales (read only), expenses, card settlements, audit log. · Sell or edit sales.
Tip: when a cashier tries a restricted action, the Manager approval needed window opens. A manager enters their credentials on the spot; the approval is valid only once, for that action.
Tip: if a page is missing from your menu, nothing is broken: your role does not give access to it. Ask the administrator.

topics.title: Choose the language
topics.text:
The app is available in English, French, Haitian Creole and Spanish. Each person chooses their language on their own device; the choice is kept for later sign-ins.
Sign-in page and till (computer): click EN, FR, HT or ES at the top right. The active button is blue.
Till on a phone: tap ⋯ (More actions), then choose the language in the list.
Admin: at the bottom of the menu, choose the language in the Language list.
Help center: the language buttons are at the top of the page.
The change is immediate, including help. The store's default language is set in Settings > General: it applies to anyone who has not made a personal choice.
Tip: product, category and payment method names stay in the language they were entered in. So you will sometimes see "Cash" or "Card".

topics.title: Notifications
topics.text:
The bell flags important events: low stock, purchase orders and expenses to approve, till, payments, devices, system. The blue number shows how many alerts are unread.
Click the bell (at the top of the till or of the admin menu).
Read the list of recent alerts. The type appears in color, for example LOW STOCK.
Click Dismiss next to an alert to mark it as read, or click Mark all as read.
Click All notifications and preferences to open the full page.
On the Notifications page:
Choose Unread or All in the list at the top.
Click Mark as read on an alert, or Mark all as read.
Under Notification preferences, check Show the unread count on the bell and, if email is set up, Also send me an e-mail for new alerts. Quiet hours (no e-mail) prevent emails at night.
Click Save.
Tip: marking an alert as read only affects you. An alert disappears for everyone when its problem is fixed (for example when the stock is replenished).
Tip: you only see alerts for your branches. A repeating alert is grouped: "85 times" shows how many times it happened.

topics.title: The till screen
topics.text:
After signing in, sales staff land on the till screen. It has three areas:
The top bar: the store, the till, the shift and the quick-access buttons.
Products (on the left): the search, the categories and the product tiles.
The cart (on the right): the customer, the salesperson, the items, the totals and the Charge button.
A sale always follows the same order:
Add the products to the cart.
Choose the customer, if needed.
Apply discounts, if needed.
Click Charge (F12).
Record the payment or payments, then click Complete sale.
Hand over the receipt and the change.

Admin · Opens the admin area (owner, administrator, manager).

topics.title: Add products and manage the cart
topics.text:
You have three ways to add a product:
Scan the barcode: the product is added to the cart automatically.
Search: type part of the name, the SKU or the barcode in Search products or scan a barcode... (F2), then click the product tile.
Browse: click a category (All, Drinks…) then the product tile.
Each tile shows the name, the variant (size, color), the SKU, the price and the stock, for example 65 in stock.
The cart, on the right, shows each line with its unit price, quantity and total.
Click + or − to change the quantity, or type it in the box.
Click the trash can to remove the line.
Click Add a note to write a remark printed on the receipt.
Click Clear cart to remove everything (you are asked to confirm).
Below the lines: the Subtotal, discounts, Tax, the Total and its equivalent in the other currency (for example ≈ in HTG).
Warning: the till never sells more than the available stock. An Out of stock tile is grayed out. If you ask for too many, a message shows the available quantity, for example "Only 3 × … in stock".
Tip: if a scanned code is unknown, the message "No product found for …" appears. Check the item or search for it by name.
Tip: on the keyboard, ↑ ↓ select a line, + and − change its quantity and Delete removes it.
Offline, searching by name, SKU or barcode also works: it uses the copy of the catalog kept on the device (see Sell offline).

topics.title: Sell a product by weight
topics.text:
Some products are sold by weight, length or volume (for example rice by the kilo).
With a scale label: scan the label. The weight or price is read from the barcode and the line is added automatically.
Without a label: click the product. The Enter the quantity window opens. Type the weight shown on the scale, for example 1.250, then click Apply.
In the cart, the line shows as "1.250 kg × US$1.20/kg". To correct the weight, click the line's quantity.
Tip: each scale label creates its own line, even for the same product.
Tip: weighed products and their unit are set up in Admin (see Units and products sold by weight). The label format is set in Scale labels.

topics.title: Customer group prices and discount
topics.text:
A customer can belong to a Group (for example Wholesalers or VIP). The group can have a Default price list and a Discount % (see Customer groups).
At the till, everything is automatic:
Choose the customer (F4).
The cart is recalculated with the prices from the group's list. A message confirms it, for example "Group Wholesalers: group prices and a 5% group discount apply."
The discount appears in the totals on the Group discount (Wholesalers, 5%) line, then on the receipt.
No approval is asked for: the store decided these prices for this group. There is no price list to choose by hand.
Tip: removing the customer (going back to walk-in) restores normal prices right away.
Warning: a cart loaded from an estimate keeps the estimate's negotiated prices (see Estimates).
Tip: products not on the group's list keep their normal price; the group's discount % still applies to them.

topics.title: Selling offline
topics.text:
The till keeps a copy of products, prices, taxes, and stock on the device. If the Internet goes down, you keep selling: each sale is saved on the device and then sent to the server as soon as the connection returns.
To sell offline, the till must have received an offline lease while it was online. It is renewed automatically when the till is connected and stays valid for a set time (24 hours by default, see Offline and security).
When the connection drops, the indicator at the top changes from Online (green) to Offline (orange). A banner may remind you of the deadline.
Scan or search for products as usual (search by name, SKU, or barcode works offline).
Click Charge.
Take cash, card, or MonCash, then click Complete sale.
The Sale complete window shows "Saved offline". The receipt has a temporary number that starts with OFFLINE-. Give it to the customer as usual.
Feature · Why
Held carts · They are kept on the server.
Gift cards (sale and payment) · The server checks the code and the balance.
Points, sale on account, store credit · The server checks the customer's balance.
Search for or create a customer · The sale continues as a walk-in customer.
Promo codes · The server validates the code.
Manager approval · It goes through the server.
Returns and voids · The Returns button is grayed out.
Warning: offline, the till does not sell more than the stock it knows about ("Only … in stock on this till (offline)"). A payment in another currency uses the rate stored on the till.
If the till stays offline too long, the screen locks: Offline selling is paused. Possible causes: the lease has expired, the device's clock went backward, or the till was deactivated. Sales already made stay safe. Reconnect, then click Try again.
Warning: a new till must be opened at least once with Internet, otherwise it cannot sell offline.

topics.title: Why is a date rejected?
topics.text:
To prevent typing mistakes, the app checks dates. Often, the calendar does not even offer the dates that are not allowed.
Where · Rule · Message
Expense: Date · Not in the future · "The expense date cannot be in the future"
Supplier invoice: Invoice date · Not in the future · "The invoice date cannot be in the future"
Supplier invoice: Due date · Not before the invoice date · "The due date cannot be before the invoice date."
Supplier payment or credit · Not in the future · "The date cannot be in the future"
Purchase order: Expected delivery · Not in the past · "The expected delivery date cannot be in the past"
Customer: date of birth · Not in the future, not before 1900 · "The date cannot be before 1900"
Discount, price list: end of validity · After the start and not in the past · "Must be after the start date", "The end date cannot be in the past"
Estimate: Valid until · Not in the past · "The valid-until date cannot be in the past"
Settings: Takes effect · In the future, or empty · "Choose a time in the future, or leave empty"
Employee: hire date · At most one year ahead · "The hire date cannot be more than a year ahead"
Employee: last day · Not in the future, not before hire · "The termination date is before the hire date"
Attendance: entered times · Not in the future, clock-out after clock-in, 24 h maximum · "The time cannot be in the future"…
Periods (reports, sales, shifts, statements) · Start ≤ end · The end cannot be before the start
Tip: a date already saved that is now in the past (for example the end of an old estimate) can be kept as is; the rule applies when you enter or change the date.
